headline: Decagon, a start-up that builds AI agents for customer support, has reportedly hired a bank to assess acquisition interest after early talks with ServiceNow and others.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a prominent AI agent start-up is exploring a sale, but the talks are early and anonymous, and ServiceNow says its own are over.
importance_line: A sale would show how much large software firms will pay for AI agent start-ups, and could change who supplies customer-support agents to companies such as Delta and Ticketmaster, but the talks are early, ServiceNow says its own are not ongoing, and Decagon could raise money instead.
summary: Business Insider reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that Decagon, whose AI agents handle customer support for companies including Delta, Snapchat and Ticketmaster and which was valued at $4.5 billion earlier this year, has hired a bank to evaluate acquisition interest and held early talks with the cloud software company ServiceNow, which a spokesperson says are no longer ongoing, along with early talks with other companies. If no deal comes, Decagon could instead raise a new funding round, and Business Insider links the interest to a shift in the AI boom in which tech companies increasingly buy their way into AI markets, citing Nvidia's purchase of Hugging Face and Stripe's purchase of OpenRouter.
notes: Read in full via fulltext; the article carries an update line that ServiceNow says it is no longer in talks.
